identity.name: Göksenin Güngör
identity.role: Lead engineer. Generalist, frontend to backend.
identity.now: Leading engineering work across the stack at a Swiss proptech.

entries.title: 500 icons, two inks
entries.summary: My site took in a pack of 500 icons and redrew it in two inks, a line and a grey dither, and the script that checks the set prints 516.

entries.title: A map of where I shot
entries.summary: resync got a map of where I shot, and 62 minutes after it began, the commits add a read of the file header, because the first read found no GPS.

entries.title: A requirements document that says no
entries.summary: Claude drafted the requirements document for my camera app in three commits and eight minutes, and it keeps what the camera can't do yet in its table, lists seven tests that could change the answers, and never got another commit while the code moved on.

entries.title: A scale with no app
entries.summary: I wanted a bathroom scale to talk to Durandal with no Xiaomi app and no account, so a 79-line program listened to its Bluetooth broadcasts, and the later recordings on the phone corrected three facts of the first one.

entries.title: Boards that assert
entries.summary: I have a script that writes the boards of Durandal's new home screen and stops when a drawing breaks a rule of the design, and with six checks and a lint it still let three problems through.

entries.title: Motion you can measure
entries.summary: I have a script that turns every screen change of Durandal into four numbers; it found four faults on its first day, and later it put a price on a change.

entries.title: Moving 43 components to another library
entries.summary: On 14 November 2026 the UI primitives of my site moved from Base UI to ui-sdk in 43 files, and I still don't know what the new parts do on touch, in Safari or with a screen reader.

entries.title: One red
entries.summary: My site has one red, for the main action and for failures, so an action that can't be undone isn't red here, and on 14 November one commit took red tints out of 20 files that broke the rule.

entries.title: One :root, three platforms
entries.summary: I wrote that one block of CSS keeps this site and my apps from drifting apart, and it turned out that no app reads the files that block writes.

entries.title: Red means your data leaves the phone
entries.summary: A review found that the new design of Durandal never said when a button is red, so the same day we wrote the rule down, and it says red only when an action sends my data out of the phone or writes to another service.

entries.title: Steps, not tweens
entries.summary: I'll show you how every motion on this site is a jump, never a tween, and how the one effect that ran for nearly ten days, the Build, was turned off with no reason on record.

entries.title: The same system, somewhere else
entries.summary: My site's design system now runs inside a theme for T3 Code and a layout for Herdr, and nothing in either repository checks that the copies still match the site.

entries.title: A design system on a TV
entries.summary: The design system of my site went onto a TV before it had a part or a rule for one, and a remote with no pointer changed how focus, a press and one grey work.

entries.title: A verdict, not a score
entries.summary: Durandal reads four signals, two of them against my own normal range of 60 days, and tells me one word, go, steady or ease, and never a score from 0 to 100.

entries.title: Nothing is written without a diff
entries.summary: I let a model draft my training routines in Durandal, but nothing reaches Hevy until a function has checked the draft and I've confirmed a diff, which comes to three write requests and no delete.

entries.title: Replacing the home screen of a TV
entries.summary: The home screen of my TV kept putting ads above my own apps, so I swapped it for a fork of an open-source Android launcher, which took one category in a file and three commands, and four things stayed out of reach.

entries.title: The wall
entries.summary: I locked a new home for Durandal with no tabs and no scroll, one wall of rooms where a room is as big as its area needs today, and I changed one of its rules the same day.

entries.title: Three ways to talk to one camera
entries.summary: My Fujifilm X-T30 II has no official SDK, so resync talks to it three ways, USB for the recipes, Bluetooth for a pocket and the camera's own Wi-Fi for the picture, and no single link does it all.

entries.title: Trending with no account
entries.summary: The big card on my TV's home screen shows what's trending with one key to a public database and no sign-in to any video app, until a Spotify feed turned up that wants an account.

entries.title: What Bluetooth can't see
entries.summary: I wanted the lock screen of resync to count my photos, but my camera doesn't tell the phone when it takes one, and the two Bluetooth experiments that went looking were reverted 29 minutes after the first one went in.

entries.title: Writing a film recipe to slot C1
entries.summary: I wanted film recipes in my Fujifilm without its phone app, and resync wrote one over USB on the first morning, until the camera answered "invalid value" to a value it had given us itself, so now every value is read back and every refusal is named.

entries.title: Personal software, again
entries.summary: I asked Claude one question about my Hevy data, and three days later I had paid Apple again and owned an iPhone PT coach called Durandal.

entries.title: Something About AI
entries.summary: This year I stopped writing code and handed the work to AI; it made me more effective, and I still miss the escaping.

entries.title: Fourteen minutes of text/x-component
entries.summary: How one test request made Cloudflare serve a Next.js RSC payload as my /writing page for about 14 minutes, and why my bypass rule lost.

entries.title: resync
entries.summary: I didn't like the phone app of my Fujifilm X-T30 II, so I had Claude build one for just that camera, and the thing I wanted on my lock screen, a photo count over Bluetooth, is the one thing the camera won't tell it.

entries.title: terminal home
entries.summary: The home screen of my Google TV showed ads, so I had Claude Code fork an open-source Android launcher into one dark screen in the design system of this site.

entries.title: Durandal
entries.summary: A personal app for my iPhone that holds eleven areas of my life on one screen. Its home is a wall of rooms, each sized by what the day needs.

entries.title: Afet Harita
entries.summary: Two weeks as a volunteer frontend engineer on the help map that thousands of volunteers built after the February 2023 earthquake in Türkiye.

entries.title: Found objects
entries.summary: Seventeen interface ideas from ui-feed.dev, built again in two inks on ui-sdk. A VCR timer, a kiln program, a flip-dot rating, a departure board, and this page's own requests.

entries.title: Aftershock
entries.summary: Every earthquake of the week, worldwide, drawn as text on a half-block map. The quakes line up along the edges of the plates.

entries.title: Background Process
entries.summary: A process that only runs while you're looking somewhere else. Leave the tab and it works in the tab's title and icon; come back and it tells you what it did.

entries.title: Majority Shell
entries.summary: One shell prompt for everyone on this page. Each of you votes for a command, and every ten seconds the shell runs the one most of you picked. Somewhere on the machine there is a key.

entries.title: Match --foreground
entries.summary: A hunt for this site's bone ink on your own screen. Pick any pixel, in any app, and see how many steps away from the colour it is.

entries.title: Pinned
entries.summary: Aftershock's seismograph in a small window that stays on top of everything else on your screen, so the week's earthquakes tick by while you work.

entries.title: Redacted
entries.summary: A short memory, blacked out line by line. Select a line to read it, but you can only hold three at once; a fourth covers the oldest again.

entries.title: Reflow
entries.summary: One column of text that runs across real browser windows. Open another with split, drag them around, and the words reflow in reading order, left to right.

entries.title: Tape
entries.summary: Shelley's Ozymandias on a teletype printout that types itself as you scroll, one character at a time, with no JavaScript. Scroll back and the paper unprints.

entries.title: Telegraph
entries.summary: One telegraph wire shared by everyone on the page. Hold the key to send Morse; whoever keys first holds the line, and everyone hears the tone and watches it decode.

entries.title: The One Red
entries.summary: This site has one red, for the one action that matters and for failure. Here everyone on the page shares one red button, and it lights only while enough of you hold it at the same time.

entries.title: Whoami
entries.summary: A neofetch of your own machine, read the way any website can read it, with no prompt and no click. The lines add up to a fingerprint, and nothing leaves your browser.

entries.title: Terminal Home
entries.summary: I took the ads off my Google TV and replaced its home screen with one built on this site's design system, with a dock of eight apps and a trending card that follows the app in focus. Use the arrow keys.

entries.title: Forty-Nine Tickets
entries.summary: Claude built all 49 tickets of grimoire in 58 hours, with six fast hours, a night of burning my usage for nothing, a post-mortem it wrote about itself, and a new plan that worked. By that evening it was on npm, and public.

entries.title: Leaving the Party
entries.summary: I left an Arc Raiders party half asleep with an idea for an issue tracker, gave Claude seven lines and my permission, and went to bed.
